name: Tabs
description: A controlled tab component supporting horizontal and vertical orientations with two visual variants: line (bottom-border indicator) and enclosed (folder-tab style). Fully keyboard accessible with arrow-key navigation.

keyboardInteraction: ArrowLeft / ArrowRight — navigate tabs in horizontal orientation
ArrowUp / ArrowDown — navigate tabs in vertical orientation
Home — move focus to first enabled tab
End — move focus to last enabled tab
Tab — move focus into the active tab panel
notes: Disabled tabs have aria-disabled="true" and are skipped in arrow-key navigation.
Each tab has a unique id and aria-controls pointing to its panel id.
Each panel has role="tabpanel", tabIndex=0, and aria-labelledby pointing to its tab id.
The tablist has aria-orientation matching the orientation prop.

tabs.type: Array<{ label: string; value: string; content: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean; artwork?: ReactNode }>
tabs.description: Array of tab definitions. Each item provides a label, a unique value, panel content, an optional disabled flag, and an optional artwork (icon) slot rendered before the label.

activeValue.description: The value of the currently active tab. This is a controlled prop — the parent must update it via onChange.

onChange.description: Called when the user activates a tab. Receives the tab's value string.

variant.description: Visual style. 'line' shows a bottom border on the active tab. 'enclosed' renders tabs as folder-style raised cards.

orientation.description: Layout direction. Affects arrow-key navigation and visual layout.

fill.description: Tab width behaviour. 'intrinsic' sizes tabs to their content. 'fixed' makes all tabs equal width.

renderAll.description: When true, all tab panels are rendered in the DOM (inactive panels hidden with CSS) for SEO purposes.

className.description: Additional CSS class names to apply to the root element.

variants.line: Default. Active tab is underlined with the primary action colour. Works on light and dark surfaces.
variants.enclosed: Active tab appears raised like a folder tab. Best used above a bordered content panel.

do: Use tabs to switch between parallel views of the same level of hierarchy.
Keep tab labels short (1–3 words) so the tablist does not overflow.
Provide an activeValue and onChange — this is a controlled component.
Ensure each tab value is unique within the set.
dont: Do not use tabs for sequential steps — use ProgressSteps instead.
Do not nest tabs inside tabs.
Do not disable all tabs simultaneously.
Do not use more than 7 tabs in a single tablist.
